(GIRISH CHATNI)
 XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT The P.S.I., of K.R.Puram Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A of IPC.
2. BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, accused had loved CW.1 and both of them got married on 02.05.2018.

It is C.C.No.51976/2022 further alleged that, thereafter,
CW.1 and accused resided at 9 th Cross, Geetha Clinic Road, Devasandra.

It is further alleged that, initially the accused and CW.1 were cordial with each other, thereafter,
the accused used to consume alcohol and abused CW.1 in filthy language, threatened her with dire consequences and also subjected her to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally.
Based on the written complaint lodged by C.W.1, CW.6 has registered the case against accused in P.S. Crime No.399/2021 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a) of IPC.
Investigating Officer/ CW.6 investigated the matter, after completion of the investigation has submitted final report against the accused for the offences punishable U/s 498(A) of IPC.
3. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offence alleged against the accused and registered the criminal case against him.
4. After registration of the case, the accused has appeared before this court and enlarged on bail as he has obtained anticipatory bail.

Copy of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to him in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C. Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
C.C.No.51976/2022
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined two witnesses out of 06 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and 2 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.07 and closed its side.
Thereafter, the accused was examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against him.
The accused has denied the same and has not produced any of either oral or documentary evidence.
6. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

sentences.text:
7. The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused was married with CW.1 on 02.05.2018, thereafter, they resided at 9th Cross, Geetha Clinic Road, Devasandra, initially the accused and CW.1 were cordial with each other, thereafter, the accused used to consume alcohol and abused CW.1 in filthy language, threatened her with dire consequences and also subjected her to C.C.No.51976/2022 cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A of IPC ?
2. What Order?
8. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 : In the Negative.
 Point No.2 : As per the final order  for the following;
 REASONS  9. POINT No.1:-
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has to prove that, the accused has subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally.

10. In order to prove the above said allegations, the prosecution has examined the IO i.e., CW.6 as PW.1, wherein, he has deposed with regard to the investigation being carried out by him from the inception of registration of case till completion of investigation and filing of final report.
11. The prosecution has examined the complainant/victim/CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, she has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned Sr.APP C.C.No.51976/2022 appearing for the State has treated the said witness as hostile and fully cross examined her, wherein, nothing was elicited from her mouth in order to prove the contents of complaint and panchanama.
12. On perusal of the ocular evidence of CW.1, she has categorically admitted that, she has got divorce from the accused and got compromised the matter with the accused.

In view of the settlement between the parties, the prayer of the learned Sr.APP for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses was came to be rejected as no purpose would be served by examining them.
Merely relying on the evidence of IO witness, it cannot be concluded that, the accused has committed the offence as alleged.
In such circumstances, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

13. On perusal of the materials on record and the oral & documentary evidence of P.W.1 and 2, as the P.W.1 has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution, the evidence on record is not at all helpful to substantiate the guilt of the accused.
Hence, there is no cogent and convincing evidence against the accused.
Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to C.C.No.51976/2022 be extended to the accused and hence, the Point Nos.1 is answered in the "Negative".
